text.p: 360 Communications Co, which provides wireless and voice data services, said Wednesday it added 98,000 net customers during the second quarter of 1997, compared with 107,000 a year ago.
For the first six months of 1997 it added 223,000 net customers compared with 202,000 in the year-ago period.
360 said its churn rate, which measures the percentage of customers who discontinue service, averaged 1.69 percent for the second quarter, down from 1.77 percent a year ago.

Earlier, it reported second quarter earnings of $0.18 a share, down from $0.21 a year ago. The company said net income was hurt by the short-term dilutive effect of its November 1996 acquisition of cellular markets from Independent Cellular Network, as well as a previously announced rate simplication changes.

"We're positioning 360 for long-term growth and success," Dennis Foster, president, said in a statement. "We expected the short-term impact on earnings, and we're on track to continue delivering strong results."
The company reported a market penetration rate of 9.77 percent for the second quarter of 1997, compared with 8.36 percent for the year-ago period.
